Based on my search, I can now explain how to pronounce "doge" properly. The pronunciation actually depends on which meaning you're referring to:

## The Historical Italian Title (Venetian Ruler)

When referring to the chief magistrate of the former republics of **Venice and Genoa**, "doge" is pronounced:

- **UK: /dəʊʒ/** — sounds like "doh-zh" (rhymes with "rogue" but with a soft 'zh' sound like in "vision")
- **US: /doʊʒ/** — same sound, "doh-zh"

This pronunciation comes from the Italian/Venetian dialect origin of the word, derived from Latin *dux* meaning "leader."

## The Internet Meme (Doge Dog)

For the famous **Shiba Inu meme** that became popular around 2013, there are actually two common pronunciations:

1. **/doʊdʒ/** — "doh-j" (rhymes with "dodge") — This is how many English speakers naturally read it
2. **/doʊɡ/** — "doh-g" (rhymes with "vogue") — Some people pronounce it this way to distinguish it from "dodge"

The meme originated from the Homestar Runner web animation series where "doge" was used as a deliberate misspelling/mispronunciation of "dog."

## Key Difference

| Meaning | Pronunciation | Sounds Like |
|---------|--------------|-------------|
| Venetian ruler | /dəʊʒ/ or /doʊʒ/ | "doh-zh" (soft 'zh' like vision) |
| Internet meme | /doʊdʒ/ or /doʊɡ/ | "doh-j" or "doh-g" |

The most important distinction is that the **historical Italian title uses the soft "zh" sound** (/ʒ/), while the **meme typically uses the hard "j" sound** (/dʒ/) similar to "dodge."

Sources:
1. https://dictionary.cambridge.org/pronunciation/english/doge
2. https://dictionary.cambridge.org/us/pronunciation/english/doge
3. https://www.collinsdictionary.com/dictionary/english/doge
4. https://memepediadankmemes.fandom.com/wiki/Doge
5. https://tieba.baidu.com/p/7611827332
6. http://italianhistories.com/podcast/venice-a-saint-comes-to-venice/
